calls.head: The Maple Leafs can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Oilers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Maple Leafs’ kill is near the bottom. The Maple Leafs need to stay out of the box. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

surprises.head: Edmonton brought the hits
surprises.body: Edmonton usually hits more than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 191 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 108 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: A rough night for Tristan Jarry
surprises.body: Jarry allowed 6 goals on 30 shots, worth 3.1 expected goals: 2.9 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 30 starts.

story.head: Nylander scores his 300th as the Maple Leafs beat the Oilers
paras: Jack Roslovic struck first for the Maple Leafs midway through the first, in his first game back in Edmonton. Auston Matthews and Troy Stecher scored 54 seconds apart early in the second to stretch the lead to 3-0. Connor Murphy and Vinni Lettieri squared off midway through the period, and Leon Draisaitl got the Oilers on the board late in the period. The third period brought five goals. William Nylander stretched the lead to 4-1 on the power play early in the period. Zack MacEwen scored his first goal for Toronto with less than seven minutes left to make it 5-1. Draisaitl scored again on the power play with three and a half minutes left to cut Toronto’s lead to 5-2, his sixth straight game with a goal. Nylander scored his 300th NHL goal into the empty net with just over two minutes left. Lettieri scored his first goal for Toronto with 31 seconds left to make it 7-2.

The chances were closer than the score. Anthony Stolarz made 30 saves for the Maple Leafs, and Tristan Jarry allowed six goals on 30 shots. By our Swing measure, Darren Raddysh had the best night of anyone. The Leafs moved to 7-4-2 and climbed to third in the Atlantic, while the Oilers fell to 8-2-1, slipping out of first in the NHL.

items.text: William Nylander passed Rick Vaive for sixth on the Maple Leafs’ all-time goals list, with 300.
The Oilers’ three-game winning streak is over.
Four straight wins for the Maple Leafs.
Connor McDavid has a point in every game this season.
